PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL - ATTORNEY-CLIENT / WORK PRODUCT
MEMORANDUM - Verdana Health Systems: HIPAA Compliance Gap Analysis (OCR Case No. 04-24-38712)
To: R. Whitmore (for C. Brennan / Audit Committee). Record as of Oct. 15, 2024; all eight supplied documents reviewed. Citations are 45 CFR unless noted.

1. BOTTOM LINE AND PRIORITIES
The program exists mostly on paper. Exposure includes willful neglect (known, uncured high-risk findings since 2022): 2024 Tier 4 range $71,162-$2,134,831 per violation, annual cap $2,134,831 (160.404; 89 Fed. Reg. Aug. 8, 2024). The subpoena letter's $63,973-$2,067,813 is stale. Priorities before Nov. 4: (1) preserve logs, stop auto-purge today; (2) make the Incident #3 breach determination now; (3) execute BAAs (NexGen first), suspend ClearView transfers; (4) commission a new risk analysis; (5) request extension in writing by Oct. 21 (10 business days before deadline); (6) fix governance and conflicts.

2. SUBPOENA STRATEGY (Categories 1-7)
- Extension: seek rolling production, priority tranches for Categories 3, 6, 7; production is continuing (Instr. 6).
- Cat. 1: manual (v2.0, Mar. 15, 2021), IRP (Sept. 2020), org charts, amendments since Jan. 1, 2022. Do not backdate or quietly "refresh"; date new policies honestly as remediation.
- Cat. 2 (from Jan. 1, 2023): Pinehurst BAA (executed Apr. 1, 2021; expires Mar. 31, 2026), SLAs, internal access-scope analyses (tracker "Pinehurst Access Review" tab; Aug. 28 notice letter), due diligence (last review June 15, 2023; likely thin).
- Cat. 3 (logs): responsive items include the Aug. 26 log review (reached about late May 2024), Pinehurst authentication records, Pinehurst-held logs (3(c)). January-May logs are gone; May-July events seen Aug. 26 may have since purged unless exported. OCR's Aug. 22 data request triggered preservation; continued purge invites adverse-inference/obstruction arguments (160.310; 18 U.S.C. 1519). Now: confirm what was exported; suspend purge; have TerraFirm seek logs in Pinehurst snapshots, Crestline and Ironbridge copies; demand Pinehurst's records under the BAA. Give the Instruction 5 lost-document statement candidly (policy six years; practice 90 days), proactively.
- Cat. 4 (from Oct. 1, 2021): Employee A terminated Apr. 22, 2023; Employee B written warning; no manager sanctioned; Pinehurst employee (BA, on leave). Collect written sanction records (164.530(e)(2)).
- Cat. 5 (from Jan. 1, 2021): June 2022 assessment, remediation tracker, Greenleaf Aug. 2024 report; no management responses documented. Confirm what Sentinel Risk Assessment Services (BAA Feb. 2022) did.
- Cat. 6: Verdana likely holds no Pinehurst training records; say so, produce any BAA training clause, request from Pinehurst. Manual has no vendor-workforce training policy.
- Cat. 7: three incidents, IRP, BCP/DR plans; no tabletops exist.
- Privilege: log per Instr. 4. Greenleaf's report (non-lawyer, annual ordinary-course audit, "not legal advice," management distribution) and the incident log (compliance business record) probably are not privileged despite labels; plan to produce. In re Capital One (E.D. Va. 2020) (persuasive) denied work-product protection to a report that would have been prepared anyway. Keep our memo and counsel communications separate; minutes labelled "Board privileged" are not protected by label.
- Irregularities (no basis to resist): letter cites 1320d-5(c) though 160.314 is the subpoena provision; signature lines blank. Cooperate (160.310), seek informal resolution (160.312).
- Posture: pair production with documented corrective action (160.408 factors; 160.410 cure defense unavailable for willful neglect uncured); "recognized security practices" (Pub. L. 116-321) likely unprovable.

3. INCIDENT #3 (PINEHURST) - CRITICAL
- No breach determination or four-factor assessment 54+ days after Aug. 22. Impermissible access is presumed a breach unless low probability of compromise is shown (164.402); a stalking ex-spouse viewing therapy notes cannot rebut. Treat as a breach.
- Clock runs from discovery, including agent knowledge (164.404(a)(2), (b)); Pinehurst's employee knew from April. From Aug. 22, 60 days ends Oct. 21; from Aug. 12 it has passed. Notify now; the log's reasons for waiting (Pinehurst's investigation, counsel engagement, "all the facts") are not legal grounds. IRP 5.3 (30-day investigation) was also ignored.
- Role issue: for VerdaCare, Verdana may be a business associate of provider practices (covered entity only via VerdaCare Premium, itself questionable). Then 164.410 notice runs to the provider covered entities (client BAAs may be shorter); check BAAs, and state mental-health and breach statutes. Whether the notes are "psychotherapy notes" (164.501) is open.
- Scope: 12 Pinehurst production admins, shared service account, no vendor-level logging; other victims plausible. Sweep all admin sessions.
- Fix: named accounts and MFA (Pinehurst has not implemented as of Oct. 15); demand its investigation; evaluate BAA remedies (164.504(e)(1)(ii)).

4. VENDOR MANAGEMENT - CRITICAL
- Pinehurst: root/DBA access to ~2.3M records; 12 production, 8 backup (single-factor VPN), 10 EHR (shared credentials), 4 super-admin accounts; unencrypted API payloads visible. Implicates 164.312(a)(1), (a)(2)(i), 164.312(d), 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(D), 164.502(b), 164.308(b), 164.314(a). Tracker says the BAA lacks access limits yet cites BAA 6.1 "minimum necessary"; read the actual BAA. Manual 9.3 required review every two years.
- 9 of 47 vendors lack valid BAAs (164.502(e), 164.308(b), 164.504(e)): expired - Summit Shredding (Apr. 2022), Beacon Staffing (Jan. 2023), Lakeview (Feb. 2023), Ashford (Aug. 2023), NexGen (June 30, 2024; ~150,000 records/yr; renewal stalled); never executed - Keystone (~180,000 records), Thornberry, Oakridge, Foxglove. Greenleaf spotlights NexGen and the minutes called this "housekeeping"; 2022-2023 lapses look like willful neglect, each disclosure a separate violation. Execute BAAs now (they do not cure past violations), consider suspending PHI flow to non-signers, assess each as impermissible disclosure. Update the 2020 template (Security Rule, subcontractor flow-down, access limits, reporting timing, audit); manual 9.2 omits Security Rule and amendment/accounting terms.

5. CLEARVIEW DE-IDENTIFICATION - CRITICAL
Safe Harbor requires 3-digit ZIPs be 000 where the area has 20,000 or fewer people (164.514(b)(2)(i)(B)); datasets did not comply, so data is PHI and a DUA-only arrangement is likely an impermissible disclosure. Transfers continued Sept. 1, 2024, after Greenleaf's Aug. 23 suspend recommendation. Suspend; recover or destroy; test limited-data-set (164.514(e)) or expert-determination (164.514(b)(1)) alternatives; check whether client BAAs let Verdana de-identify or disclose (164.504(e)(2)(i)); run breach assessment.

6. INCIDENT #2 (LAPTOP) - HIGH
Discovery Nov. 17, 2023; HHS Jan. 28, 2024 (72 days); individuals Feb. 3 (78 days); limit Jan. 16 (164.404(b), 164.408(b)). Delay was process (draft Dec. 15; legal review Jan. 8-22), not complexity. No media notice (164.406, more than 500 residents of a state; confirm counts) or substitute-notice analysis. Root cause: unremediated 2022 encryption finding; local PHI storage contrary to manual 14.3; 87 of 104 laptops encrypted now. ~1,100 SSNs; check state deadlines. Log date error: Nov. 17, 2023 was a Friday, not "Monday."

7. INCIDENT #1 (SNOOPING) - HIGH
Billing employee (the email says clinical; reconcile) accessed 14 records incl. a public figure; found after about 45 days; "low probability" decided verbally, no written four-factor assessment (164.402(2); 164.414(b) burden). Curiosity access fits no 164.402(1) exception; termination does not negate compromise. Likely breach: individual notice (about June 13, 2023) and HHS small-breach log (about Feb. 29, 2024) missed. Do a documented retrospective assessment and consider late notices. GC learned after the decision; CTO excluded; access review requested April 2023, never done; 215 Clinical Support users still see all records; no retraining after any incident.

8. RISK ANALYSIS - CRITICAL
Last enterprise analysis June 2022 (28 months); 10 of 23 findings open including encryption (~38 legacy installs), admin MFA, log retention, with no plan or risk acceptance (164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A)-(B), (a)(8), 164.312(a)(2)(iv), (d)). Two incidents trace to these items. Commission now through counsel, preferably not Greenleaf (did the 2022 assessment, seeks remediation work, is also financial auditor and a BAA-tracker vendor rated "Low"). Build an owned remediation register reporting to the Audit Committee.

9. AUDIT LOGS - CRITICAL
Ninety days violates manual 11.3/20.2 (six years). Precision: 164.316(b)(2) and 164.530(j) cover required documentation; 164.312(b) and 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(D) require audit controls and review, not an express log period, so Greenleaf's regulatory framing is overstated; the clear breach is Verdana's own policy plus weak monitoring (quarterly review; six Pinehurst events undetected). Reconfigure retention, add alerting.

10. GOVERNANCE AND CONFLICTS - HIGH
- Liang did not know she is Security Officer, never attended committees (164.308(a)(2)); designate a functioning officer. IRP still names Hargrove (left Nov. 2022); Tilford acts informally.
- Privacy Officer uncredentialed, unaware of HITECH rights; 4 FTEs for 1,247 employees, 14 states, 2.3M records.
- CCO reports to GC; 40% revenue-linked bonus (approved Mar. 21, 2024 over Rutherford's concern). OIG guidance (2023) expects independence: reporting line to Audit Committee, remove revenue metrics.
- Compliance absent from Q2/Q3 2024 agendas; Ridgeline's June 2024 IRP/tabletop recommendation not acted on. On Sept. 19 the Committee heard Greenleaf's seven Critical findings described as improvements, with no report circulated and no mention of the OCR complaint, Aug. 22 request or Pinehurst; brief the Committee fully now (Caremark-type exposure).
- Counsel conflict: Ms. Brennan is a fact witness (Committee member, manual signatory, BAA template owner, 14-day Incident #2 review, delay decision on Incident #3). Report also to the Audit Committee chair, use Upjohn warnings, evaluate separate counsel for individuals.
- Compliance Committee omits the Privacy and Security Officers; request Sept. 30 minutes.

11. POLICIES AND TRAINING - HIGH
- Manual stale since Mar. 15, 2021 (164.530(i)); names Hargrove; broken cross-references; says HHS notified "simultaneously" (17.6) versus 60 days (18.2); hotline numbers conflict.
- Minimum necessary covers paper only (12.2) (164.502(b), 164.514(d)).
- No BYOD policy for 312 personal phones (164.310(d), 164.312); manual 14.4 covers Company devices only.
- Tracking: no policy; two analytics tools on authenticated portal. AHA v. Becerra (N.D. Tex. June 20, 2024) vacated the bulletin's unauthenticated-page "proscribed combination"; OCR dropped its appeal Aug. 29, 2024; authenticated use remains risky. Assess FTC Health Breach Notification Rule.
- Restrictions: manual 7.4 omits out-of-pocket restrictions (164.522(a)(1)(vi)); confirm applicability to Verdana's role.
- Training: unchanged since 2021, no telehealth content, one module for all (843 PHI users) (164.530(b); 164.308(a)(5)); 91% completion (about 112 untrained); new hires average 67 days versus 30 (6 of 23 timely).
- Greenleaf cites the 2024 reproductive-health rule, since vacated (Purl v. HHS, N.D. Tex. June 18, 2025); verify status. No 14-state law analysis exists; commission one.

12. IRP - HIGH
Never reviewed or tested (164.308(a)(6)); no risk-assessment form; log categories A-D differ from IRP A-E; claims "comprehensive audit logging"; TerraFirm/Ridgeline unverified. Rewrite with 60-day hard stop, decision log, panel, tabletop within 60 days.

13. DOCUMENT INCONSISTENCIES
- Greenleaf (dated Aug. 23) references the Oct. 3 subpoena and "pending" OCR matter though interviews ended July 15: revised after issuance or misdated; OCR will ask.
- Greenleaf summary (5/7/4/2) conflicts with matrix (7/9/2/0).
- Log availability stated as April, May, late May, early July.
- Practices: 480 versus ~310. Email says 30 days; window is 32.

14. ROADMAP
0-14 days: hold; breach determination/notices; extension; BAAs; ClearView suspension; Committee briefing; Pinehurst named accounts/MFA; Security Officer; privilege protocol.
15-30: production tranches; risk analysis; interim IRP; retention fix.
31-90: MFA, encryption, role-based access, BYOD/MDM, manual rewrite, tiered training, tabletop, vendor gate, CCO reporting.
90-180: re-paper vendors; state-law review; validation.

15. UNRESOLVED
Pinehurst BAA text; exports made Aug. 26; CE/BA role; client BAAs; state counts; Sept. 30 minutes; sanction files. eCFR was inaccessible, so rule citations need cite-checking.
